subject: [BrightCart] Urgent: hosted API p99 spike — status page communications & corrective plan
body:
--- Message 1 / 7 ---
From: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@brightcart.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 27 Feb 2027 22:14:03 -0800
Subject: [BrightCart] Elevated p99 and intermittent 503s since 21:00 PT

Evelyn —

We're seeing a 3x jump in p99 latency on the hosted /v1/generate endpoint starting ~21:00 PT. 503 spikes correlate with the p99 windows. Our checkout flows are being affected (saw a ~2% conversion impact in the last hour). Attaching a screenshot of the last 503 cluster. Can you confirm this is on Redwood's side and whether there's an ETA for mitigation?

We're relying on the hosted API for peak traffic; this is high severity for us.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Chen
SRE, BrightCart
attachments: screenshot-503.png

--- Message 2 / 7 ---
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 27 Feb 2027 22:24:11 -0800
Subject: Fwd: [BrightCart] Elevated p99 and intermittent 503s since 21:00 PT

Team — escalating from BrightCart. Key facts: p99 and some 503s on hosted /v1/generate since ~21:00 PT; customer reports conversion impact. They've attached screenshot.

Immediate asks:
- Marcus: can you check current model variants serving this tenant + queue lengths on the EU/US pools?
- Markus: do we have throttles or routing fallbacks tripped for BrightCart?
- Dylan: please pull p95/p99 query results for the last 3 hours (token-level breakdown) and share ASAP.

I'll keep BrightCart updated — what's our ETA on a mitigation plan? If we need to post an incident note on status, I'm ready to coordinate copy.

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Account Lead, Hosted API — Redwood Inference

--- Message 3 / 7 ---
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 27 Feb 2027 22:36:58 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: [BrightCart] Elevated p99 and intermittent 503s since 21:00 PT

Confirming I'm on it. Quick triage:
- US-hosted pool for gen models is showing higher-than-normal queue depth for seq_len > 1024.
- Autoscaler is healthy but backpressure is visible on the GPU inference nodes for the gpt-medium-32q variant.
- No global routing fallback triggered yet.

I'll drop the first query export in 10m. If we need an immediate mitigation, we can temporarily route BrightCart to the gpt-medium-16q quant variant (slightly lower accuracy but much better latency under this load).

-Marcus

--- Message 4 / 7 ---
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 27 Feb 2027 22:47:02 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: [BrightCart] Elevated p99 and intermittent 503s since 21:00 PT

Attaching the p95/p99 export for 18:00–22:30 PT with token-level buckets. Observations: p95 is elevated ~1.4x baseline; p99 shows a 3.1x spike concentrated in requests that hit sequence lengths >1024 and when KV cache hits are below 20%. There's also a small cluster of 503s that align with two pods that restarted around 21:12 PT.

attachments: p95-p99-query-results.csv

Suggested immediate actions:
1) Route BrightCart traffic to gpt-medium-16q variant (can be done via routing policy) — expected p99 improvement ~40%.
2) Evict the two restarted pods from the pool and bring new warm pods to replace them (to avoid repeated restarts).
3) Post a brief incident entry on status.redwood.com noting elevated latencies and a targeted mitigation.

--- Message 5 / 7 ---
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@brightcart.com>
Date: Sat, 27 Feb 2027 22:59:30 -0800
Subject: Re: [BrightCart] Elevated p99 and intermittent 503s since 21:00 PT

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for flagging, and apologies for the impact. Quick update: we've identified two restarted pods in the US pool that correlate with the 503s and a queue build on longer-sequence requests. We're initiating a temporary routing change for your tenant to use a lower-latency quant variant; this should reduce p99 significantly while we stabilize the pool.

I'll post a short incident note on our public status page and follow up with a technical postmortem within 48 hours.

-Evelyn
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

--- Message 6 / 7 ---
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 00:12:05 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: [BrightCart] Elevated p99 and intermittent 503s since 21:00 PT

Thanks for the quick triage. Status actions we've taken:
- Temporary routing policy applied for tenant: BRIGHT-CUST-21 -> gpt-medium-16q (applied 22:50 PT).
- Marked the two suspect pods for replacement; new warm pods are healthy as of 23:05 PT.
- Posted an incident stub on status.redwood.com with customer-friendly language (link below).

Planned follow-ups:
- Incident postmortem draft (root cause: pod instability + workload shift toward long sequences) — will circulate for review today.
- Alongside Ops/Runtime we'll evaluate whether we need a routing policy change to prefer quant variants under queue pressure.

Link to incident note: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/INC-2027-02-28-hostedapi-latency

-Markus K.
Chief of Ops, Redwood Inference
attachments: draft-statuspage-note.md

--- Message 7 / 7 ---
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@brightcart.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 15:42:10 -0800
Subject: RE: [BrightCart] Elevated p99 and intermittent 503s since 21:00 PT — post-incident update

Hi Sarah —

Following up with a brief status and next steps after last night's event:

What happened (TL;DR): a sudden workload shift toward longer sequences (>1024 tokens) plus two unstable pods caused queueing and intermittent 503s. The combination produced a p99 regression for a window between ~21:00–23:00 PT.

What we did:
- Immediate mitigation: routed BrightCart to a lower-latency quant variant at 22:50 PT which reduced p99 by ~38% for your traffic.
- Pod replacement: we removed two unstable pods and brought warm replacements; no further restarts since 23:05 PT.
- Status page: we published an incident stub during the event and updated it with mitigation notes. Link: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/INC-2027-02-28-hostedapi-latency

Next steps / postmortem actions:
1) Root cause postmortem (ops + runtime) — scheduled today; I'll circulate the draft and action items.
2) Short-term: evaluate routing policy to prefer quant variants when queue depth > X for critical tenants.
3) Medium-term: improve pod health detection and add an automatic pod warm replacement flow to avoid repeated restart clusters.
4) Compensation: If you want, we can review usage during the impacted window and discuss a goodwill credit for the conversion impact — I can loop in Billing if helpful.

If you have any outstanding issues or still see increased latency, please ping me directly and we'll prioritize. Appreciate your patience — we'll follow up with a postmortem within 48 hours.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Account Lead, Hosted API — Redwood Inference

--- End of thread ---
